title: Pick a standard exception or a custom one for each seat-booking failure

blocks.text: Reuse a standard exception when it describes the error; create a custom one when the error belongs to your domain and callers need to tell it apart, or when it must carry data. Write `SeatMap` with seats numbered `1` to `capacity`:

items: `void reserve(int seat) throws SeatTakenException`, and its failures:

blocks.text: `reserve(3)` on a fresh `new SeatMap(10)` reserves seat 3; a second `reserve(3)` throws `SeatTakenException` with `getSeat() == 3`.
Each failure has a different cause: a bug in the caller, an object in the wrong state, or a business rule a caller can recover from. Choose the type that says which.

cases.says: Free seats in range can be reserved, and isReserved reports them.
A taken seat is the domain's own SeatTakenException, carrying the seat number for the caller to offer another.
A seat number outside 1..capacity is a plain IllegalArgumentException naming the number, not an array index error.
Reserving after close() is an IllegalStateException: the argument is fine, the object is not ready.

concepts: A custom exception is worth creating when the error is part of the domain and callers must tell it apart.
Standard exceptions such as IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException are reused when they describe the error.
